items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XV, List of Answers on Topics 1:1
items.html: (To the question) Every degree receives only from its immediate upper one, and ZA is the upper one of Malchut; therefore she cannot receive anything except from ZA. (Item 2).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XV, List of Answers on Topics 2:1
items.html: In the Ibur of the Gadlut of ZA, when he raises his AHAP with him to Aba and Ima, also the aspect of the bodies of Malchut is attached to the AHAP of ZA, and she is discerned as her first MAN. Therefore, in this Ibur, two statures of ten Sefirot then emerge: one upon his MAN, and one upon the MAN of the Nukva. And since the Nukva is not fit to receive there her stature of ten Sefirot, because they are of the upper ones, therefore ZA receives her stature in deposit, in the secret of the firstborn taking a double portion. And afterward, when ZA descends from there and comes to his place, he returns to her the stature of ten Sefirot that he received on her behalf, little by little, in the manner of the degree, as is known.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XV, List of Answers on Topics 2:2
items.html: (To the question) And it is found that as long as Malchut has not received her deposit from ZA, her stature of ten Sefirot is still included in ZA. Behold, prior to the growth of Malchut, her nine Sefirot are found included in ZA. (Item 3).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XV, List of Answers on Topics 3:1
items.html: In the shattering of the vessels of Nekudim, inner vessels and posterior vessels are discerned there: for the seven kings that emerged in the smallness of Nekudim, by the looking of the eyes into the AHAP, which are the vessels KHB HGT up to the chest, which from the aspect of the lights are discerned as HGT NHY, are discerned as inner vessels, and are discerned as the essence of their very selves there, for they all emerged above the Parsa, and they are Atzilut from their root. And the aspect of the vessels from the chest and below, at the time of the smallness, received no light at all, because due to the sight of the eyes they went out beyond Atzilut and were diminished to BYA, below the Parsa; but only at the time of the greatness of Nekudim, by the MAN of the Vav and the point of the Yesod of AK in Aba and Ima of Nekudim, they returned and joined to the seven kings. Therefore the seven kings spread there also into BYA, up to the point of this world, as said in Part 7. They are called the posterior vessels of Nekudim.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XV, List of Answers on Topics 3:2
items.html: (To the question) And the discernment between them is immense, for the inner vessels are, from their root, an aspect of complete Atzilut, as above; therefore they did not need to be shattered at all, and all their shattering was because, at the time of the greatness, they joined with the posterior vessels into a single Partzuf, since those vessels had already been diminished to the aspect of BYA. Therefore the inner vessels were also shattered, as said there. And hence, at the time of correction in the world of Atzilut, after the inner vessels returned and were clarified once again from their mixture with the posterior vessels, and rose and were corrected in Atzilut as before, at the time of the smallness of Nekudim, no diminishment will ever occur in them again. For this matter that was in Nekudim — namely, that the Parsa under Atzilut was nullified and the seven kings spread into BYA — will not occur again in Atzilut, for here the Parsa was corrected in a fixed manner, so that it will not be nullified even at the time of the coming of the Mochin of the Gadlut, as is known. Therefore they remain in Atzilut permanently. And they are the stature of HGT NHY of ZA, in which there is no diminishment ever. And the aspect of the point below the Yesod of ZA, which is the aspect of the Nukva of ZA, in which also no diminishment will ever occur, for she too is an aspect of an inner point, namely the Malchut of the inner vessels. Therefore her root is preserved in ZA forever. And it is known that, from the aspect of the vessels, this point is discerned as being below the chest of ZA, because from the aspect of the vessels the VAK, which are KHB HGT up to the chest, are discerned, and the point of the chest is the root of the Nukva. But from the aspect of the lights, in which the VAK are discerned as HGT NHY, the point is discerned as being below the Yesod. (Item 5).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XV, List of Answers on Topics 4:1
items.html: (To the question) It is impossible that both of them use a single Keter face to face, unless the Malchut of the first restriction, hidden in RADLA, is revealed — she being the MAN of the Nukva from the first restriction, fit for a face-to-face coupling with ZA in an equal stature. But beforehand, there is revealed in RADLA only the aspect of the Yesod of the Malchut of the first restriction, which suffices for the Mochin of the male, that is ZA, who needs only male MAN, namely the aspect of the Nukva included in the male, called the aspect of Benjamin included in Joseph. Not so the Nukva, who needs true feminine MAN, which is only the aspect of Malchut by itself. And there is no aspect of Malchut in Atzilut but only from the second restriction, called the Malchut of Ima, from which aspect there is no coupling of Gadlut, but only from the aspect of the inclusion with the crown of Gevura of ZA. There is also, in this Malchut, an aspect of a coupling of Gadlut; but since the GAR of the Nukva are not from herself, but from her inclusion in the crown of Gevura of ZA, she is already discerned as smaller than him, for she needs him for the aspect of the inclusion; therefore she is smaller than him. It is thus found that a coupling of Gadlut face to face in a single Keter is not conceivable unless she has MAN of the first restriction, upon which the Mochin of the GAR emerge. And this will not be in the aspect of the feminine MAN belonging to the Nukva, for it is hidden in RADLA and will not be revealed except in the future, in the secret of the cornerstone, as is known. (Item 5).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XV, List of Answers on Topics 5:1
items.html: The upper aspect of the stature of the Mochin is called Keter, and it depends on the lower aspect of the coarseness of the vessels, which is the screen, in such a way that if two degrees have the measure of a single MAN, their Keter is also one, as stated in the previous parts. And it is known that the growth of the Nukva throughout the whole back of ZA up to his Keter, which was on the fourth day of the work of creation, was made by the inclusion of the Hod of AA in his Netzach, by which the Nukva received the measure of the Nukva of the body of ZA, and she became the aspect of Malchut of Netzach like him, as above in Answer 6, see there. Therefore the Nukva became fit to use those male MAN of ZA, like the Nukva in the body of ZA; hence she was able to receive the Binot and Gevurot of the Aba and Ima of the AB of the Mazal, like him, which are in an equal stature with the Hochma and Hassadim of the Aba and Ima of the AB of the Mazal. In this she is found with ZA in a single Keter indeed, for since their MAN are a single aspect, namely the Malchut of Netzach, which is the aspect of the male MAN drawn from the Mazal VeNotzer, it is inevitable that their Keter is also one, namely the upper aspect of the Mochin, which is the height of the Mochin, as above. And this is what the Nukva argued: it is impossible that two kings use a single Keter, as above in Answer 6, see there.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XV, List of Answers on Topics 5:2
items.html: (To the question) And know that this measure of a single Keter operates constantly in Aba and Ima, and this is the secret of they emerge together and abide together. And this is because they are always in the aspect of a single MAN: if permanently, they are both in the aspect of the MAN of the coarseness of Behina Bet; and if in the aspect of AB, they are both in the aspect of the MAN of the Mazalot, which is the male MAN that serves for both of them. Therefore they are always in a single Keter, for at the time that they have the measure of a single MAN, they also necessarily have a single Keter, as above. And remember this. And what is said in Section 63, that his Keter is higher than her Keter, is because, in the aspect of Aba, he is discerned as though he did not emerge from the head of AA, as above, 141. (Item 5).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XV, List of Answers on Topics 6:1
items.html: (To the question) See the adjacent answer.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XV, List of Answers on Topics 7:1
items.html: Since the Mochin were divided between ZA and the Nukva — the right side, which is Hochma and Hesed, became Makifim over ZA, and the Nukva took only the aspect of the left side of the Mochin, namely the Binot and Gevurot alone, like the upper Ima herself — these Mochin are discerned as an aspect of Hochma without Hassadim, like the upper Ima at the time she ascends to AB and returns to be Hochma, in whom there is then only the aspect of Hochma alone, without Hassadim, that is, in the measure of the Hochma of the direct light. See above in Part 1, Page 5, s.v. and the reason.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XV, List of Answers on Topics 7:2
items.html: (To the question) And behold, the Bina that returned to be Hochma does not need there the aspect of Hassadim, for Bina is the very essence of Hochma from the root of its emanation in the direct light, being an aspect of expansion from the Hochma of the direct light in the root of its emanation. Therefore the light of Ein Sof clothes in her through the Hochma, and nothing more is needed. Not so ZON, who are the expansion of the Hassadim from Bina, from the very essence of their emanation, except that there is in them an illumination of the light of Hochma, as above in Page 5, s.v. and the reason. If so, Hochma is not received in them except by clothing within the Hassadim, as the Rav wrote in Shaar HaKavanot, on Yom Kippur, see there. Therefore the Nukva could not use a single Keter with ZA, for she could not stand in those Mochin, since she was lacking Hassadim: for ZA received Hochma and Hesed as Makifim, and in the Mochin there was only Binot and Gevurot alone, namely Hochma without Hassadim. Therefore also the Hochma was not clothed in them as it should be. And she requested of the Emanator that He bestow upon her an influx of Hassadim, so that the Hochma would clothe in them; then it was said to her, go and diminish yourself, meaning that she return to the point below the Yesod, and come a second time in Ibur, Yenika, and Mochin, from the Hesed of face to face, so that she would receive the Mochin upon feminine MAN; then she would have the aspect of Hochma and Hassadim together, as they are in ZA. (Item 5).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XV, List of Answers on Topics 8:1
items.html: (To the question) The Mochin that come for the completion of the vessels are discerned as lights of BAN, for the whole correction of the vessels revolves only upon the vessels that already served at the time of the greatness of Nekudim, before their shattering, when they were discerned as vessels of SAG, as is known. And after they came to receive their correction from the Mochin of the new MAH in Atzilut, they received on account of this the name BAN, as is known. Therefore all the lights of MAH that serve only for the correction of the vessels are called only BAN. And there is no MAH in the Partzuf until it is fit to couple by itself and draw, by its own MAN, the stature of MAH; and this is only after the completion of the Partzuf entirely. Thus the aspect of VAK is always called by the name lights of BAN, and even the Mochin of VAK — meaning that they come to raise the AHAP to the Partzuf and complete it with the lower thirds of every Sefira, whereby the HGT become KHB, the NHY become HGT, and new NHY emerge to it, and it is completed in ten vessels, as is known. Therefore, even though the Mochin of VAK are, from their root, an aspect of complete AB, nevertheless they are discerned only as the aspect of 216, and of the aspect of AB of SAG, MAH, BAN, which are the lights of BAN, as is known, for they come only for the completion of the vessels alone, because there is no longer any MAN in the Partzuf from the aspect of the Gadlut to draw Mochin of MAH; this comes only after it no longer needs any correction in its vessels. (Items 64 to 67).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XV, List of Answers on Topics 9:1
items.html: (To the question) All the statures of Atzilut are discerned by the name of the general MAH, and all the vessels that served in Nekudim, with the lights clothing in them for their correction, are called by the name of the general BAN. (Item 158).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XV, List of Answers on Topics 10:1
items.html: (To the question) Every lower one is discerned as being from above downward toward its upper one, and it clothes upon the body of the upper one. And there is a difference between the Partzufim of AK and the Partzufim of the GAR of Atzilut, on the one hand, and the Partzufim of ZON of Atzilut, on the other. For in AK and in the GAR, each one holds onto all the ten Sefirot of the head of its upper one, and therefore clothes the whole body of its upper one, from its mouth and below. But ZON do not hold onto all the ten Sefirot of the head of Aba and Ima, but only onto the NHY of the head of Aba and Ima alone, for in the KHB HGT of Aba and Ima they have no share, for there is the aspect of concealed Hassadim, as said at length above, Part 1, Page 667, Answer 176. Therefore the aspect of from above downward of Aba and Ima, which ZON clothe, does not clothe the whole body of Aba and Ima, but only from the chest and below — namely, to the same extent that it holds onto the heads of Aba and Ima, so does it clothe in their body. Hence the lower third of the Tifferet of Ima is the aspect of the Keter of ZA. See there in the above-mentioned answer, where this is explained at length. (Item 6).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XV, List of Answers on Topics 11:1
items.html: (To the question) When Aba and Ima are in the stature of SAG, the Keter of Aba is found higher than the Keter of Ima, for Ima, who is Bina, is discerned as having emerged from the head of AA; but the aspect of Aba did not emerge from the head of AA, from the root of his emanation. However, when they are in the stature of AB, when Bina also returns to the head of AA, then they are equal to one another. (Item 6 and in the Inner Light, s.v. and there is no).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XV, List of Answers on Topics 12:1
items.html: (To the question) Four including aspects are discerned in every Partzuf, and they are: Ibur, Yenika, Mochin, and Keter. (Item 7).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XV, List of Answers on Topics 13:1
items.html: (To the question) The third aspect is Mochin. And if in the posterior Partzufim, they are Mochin of VAK, for all the Ibur, Yenika, and Mochin of the posterior are only VAK outward, being only the completion of the vessels. And there are two aspects in these Mochin: if from the upper Aba and Ima, then from them is the aspect of the Mochin in their place; and if from YESHSUT, they are only the aspect of the illumination of the head from above downward, namely by the bowing of the head of ZA down to the place of his HGT, and the Nukva takes the Mochin from the place of the HGT. (Item 16).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XV, List of Answers on Topics 14:1
items.html: (To the question) They are the aspect of the illumination of the head from above downward, as above in Answer 143. And there is no difference in this between face to face and back to back, for in both the lower one does not receive them in the place of the head, but by the bowing of the head down to the place of the HGT, and the lower one takes them from the place of the HGT. (Item 12).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XV, List of Answers on Topics 15:1
items.html: (To the question) They are the aspect of the Mochin that the lower one receives in the place of their emergence, namely in the head of the upper one. For the Ibur of ZA is made in the place of the head of Aba and Ima, who stand in the GAR of AA; therefore, when he is born from there, he clothes from the mouth and below of AA. And likewise the Nukva is found there, receiving the Mochin from the place of the head of ZA; therefore she is with him in an equal stature. (Item 12).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XV, List of Answers on Topics 16:1
items.html: (To the question) These seven aspects that the Rav counts include all the changes of the principal states that there are in the Nukva. For first he counts the Ibur, Yenika, and Mochin of the posterior, which are the first three aspects. Then he counts the fourth aspect, which is the Yenika of the front. Then he counts the two aspects of the Mochin of Aba and Ima and of YESHSUT: the Mochin of YESHSUT of the front he counts as the fifth degree, and the Mochin of the front from Aba and Ima he counts as the sixth degree; and both of them using a single Keter face to face he counts as the seventh degree. (Item 108).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XV, List of Answers on Topics 17:1
items.html: (To the question) The seventh aspect, which is Keter, is not a degree in itself, for it comes together with the Mochin. And what he counts the seventh degree as a degree in itself is because it does not operate in this time. But in YESHSUT it operates also in this time, namely on Rosh Chodesh and on Yom Tov, as is known; therefore he does not count it separately.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XV, List of Answers on Topics 18:1
items.html: (To the question) The discussion is only about the matter of both of them using a single Keter, namely that they be in a coupling in an equal stature up to the Keter. However, in back to back, even though the Nukva ascends with ZA into a single Keter, as on Yom Kippur at Neila, nevertheless there is no coupling between them then; therefore it is not included in this degree.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XV, List of Answers on Topics 19:1
items.html: (To the question) In the Mochin of the posterior she has no aspect of her own MAN, namely feminine MAN, from the aspect of Malchut. And her Mochin are drawn from the male MAN of the Dikna, namely from the aspect of the MAN of the Ima of the AB of the Mazal; and these NHY of Ima clothe in her together with the Mochin. But in the Mochin of the front she has an aspect of her own feminine MAN, namely from the aspect of Malchut that is drawn to her from the Malchut of Ima, which is not included in her NHY of the Mazal, and is clothed in the Mochin of ZA; and there, in the head of ZA, a special coupling is made upon her, for the sake of the Mochin of the Nukva. And these Mochin clothe in the NHY of ZA, which become Mochin for the Nukva. Thus the Mochin of the posterior emerge from the Aba and Ima of AB, who clothe the GAR of AA and couple upon the MAN of the Mazal, from which the Mochin of ZA come. But the Mochin of the front of the Nukva emerge from the coupling made in the head of ZA, and they have from the aspect of the Mochin of the Mazal only a mere illumination, by the crown of Gevura of ZA.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XV, List of Answers on Topics 20:1
items.html: (To the question) The NHY of the Ima of the AB of the Mazal, which clothe in the Nukva when she is back to back, in an equal stature with ZA — behold, also the NHY of Aba are included in them; and the aspect of the Malchut of Aba, which is in his Yesod, shines outside the Yesod of the Nukva, and it is the aspect of the long Yesod of Aba, meaning the aspect of Hochma that shines there, for the illumination of Hochma is called long, as is known. And this has already been explained above in Answer 63, see there.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XV, List of Answers on Topics 21:1
items.html: (To the question) For Aba and Ima are always in the aspect of a single stature, and permanently they are in the stature of SAG, which is the aspect of the Bina of AA that went out beyond the head of AA. And by the ascent of the MAN of ZA, the Bina of AA returns to the head, and then Aba and Ima also ascend to the aspect of the GAR of AA. And they emerge together means: at the time that Bina emerged from the head of AA, then both of them also emerged from the head of AA, and they are in the aspect of SAG. And they abide together means: at the time of the return of Bina to its head, they also ascend to the head of AA and both acquire the stature of AB. Thus their stature is always equal, for they are always a single stature.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XV, List of Answers on Topics 22:1
items.html: The stature of the Nukva: behold, her place of emergence is in the head of ZA, upon the aspect of the Malchut of Ima, which is not included in the Mochin of ZA for the sake of his own Mochin. And upon this Malchut of Ima, in its inclusion with the crown of Gevura that is in the head of ZA, the Mochin of the Nukva emerge. And behold, this Malchut of Ima, upon which the Nukva holds, is not fit for Mochin, for it is the aspect of the second restriction; and the Mochin that emerge upon her are only through her inclusion in the crown of Gevura of ZA. Therefore she is discerned as needing ZA, namely the illumination of his crown of Gevura, for without this illumination she has no Mochin of the GAR. Hence she is smaller than him, for her Mochin are an offshoot of his Mochin, and come by means of their illumination, as above.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XV, List of Answers on Topics 22:2
items.html: (To the question) However, the Mochin that she receives when she is in the back of ZA, which complete her stature equally with ZA from his back — behold, their place of emergence is in the Aba and Ima of AB, who are in the place of the GAR of AA, namely in that same place where ZA also receives his Mochin, and they are not at all from the aspect of the head of ZA. Therefore she does not need him — that is, she does not need to receive the illumination of his crown of Gevura, for she receives from the upper Ima herself, like ZA.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XV, List of Answers on Topics 28:1
items.html: (To the question) The Mochin that the lower one receives from the upper one are clothed in the NHY of the upper one, as said in the previous parts. Therefore, in the Mochin of face to face, which the Nukva receives from the coupling made in the head of ZA, her Mochin come there clothed in the NHY of ZA. And in the Mochin of the posterior, which come at the time of the separation, which the Nukva receives from the coupling made in Aba and Ima, she therefore receives them in the NHY of Ima.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XV, List of Answers on Topics 29:1
items.html: (To the question) See above, Answer 19. (Item 136).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XV, List of Answers on Topics 30:1
items.html: (To the question) When she receives in the manner of the degree, namely from ZA, she is in her own house, for then the Mochin emerge upon her MAN, which is from the aspect of Malchut. But in the Mochin of the separation, which she receives from the upper Aba and Ima, who are the upper one of ZA, there it is discerned as the permission of the groom. Also, the MAN of these Mochin are the aspect of male MAN, from the aspect of the Yesod of Malchut, which is the aspect of Benjamin included in Joseph, and not the aspect of the MAN of Malchut that are particular to herself. And for these two reasons, these Mochin that she receives are discerned as from the permission of the groom, and not from the aspect of her own house.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XV, List of Answers on Topics 31:1
items.html: (To the question) Only the Mochin of face to face are drawn from the head of ZA, as the Rav wrote above in Item 138, see there. But the Mochin of the separation, which come in the back, are drawn from Aba and Ima themselves, equally with the Mochin of ZA.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XV, List of Answers on Topics 32:1
items.html: (To the question) In the permission of the groom, which is the upper Aba and Ima, her Mochin are equal to the Mochin of ZA, for ZA receives there the aspect of the Mochin of Aba, and the Nukva receives there the Mochin of Ima; and their statures are found equal. But in the house of the Nukva, she receives the Mochin in the manner of the degree, namely from the coupling made in the head of ZA, and she does not have the root of the Gevurot themselves, namely the male Gevurot that come from the first restriction, but only the aspect of the Gevurot of the Malchut of Ima, which is the aspect of the second restriction — except that she receives an illumination from the crown of Gevura of ZA, which is the aspect of the root of the Gevurot. And since now she needs the illumination of the Gevurot of ZA, and she is an offshoot of his Mochin, therefore both of them do not use a single Keter.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XV, List of Answers on Topics 33:1
items.html: (To the question) The Mochin of the front she receives from the Malchut of Ima, as above, Part 14, Answer 90, see there. And the Mochin of the posterior, of an equal stature with ZA, she receives from the NHY of Ima.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XV, List of Answers on Topics 34:1

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XV, List of Answers on Topics 35:1
items.html: (To the question) In the Mochin of face to face the Nukva receives from the left of AA, and in the Mochin of the separation, which are the Mochin of the posterior, she receives from the Netzach of AA, by the inclusion of the Netzach in his Hod.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XV, List of Answers on Topics 36:1
